content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, adding further football coverage and offering tennis fans new ways to follow multiple major tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds multiple football leagues and tennis schedules

When Apple first launched the Apple Sports app, the experience was quite limited in terms of both supported regions and sports covered.

Since then, the app has made significant progress on both fronts, expanding to over 170 countries and regions, and continuously adding support for new sports, leagues, and tournaments.

For example, earlier this year, Apple Sports expanded to 90 new countries and introduced several new features around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports has been updated again, adding Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier League to its football lineup.

Additionally, the app now also allows tennis fans to "track tournament draws in real time (...), including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," Apple said, noting that users can "see matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Here is the full changelog for Apple Sports 4.4:

Football coverage continues to expand with the addition of Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier League. Tennis fans can track tournament draws in real time on Apple Sports, including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events, making it easy to follow matchups and results for each round.

Are you using Apple Sports? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
